description: Read and search an Obsidian vault. Provides hybrid search, tag queries, and a structured memory layer (About Me/) for personalization across conversations.
instructions:
Read and search an Obsidian vault. Use vault_search and vault_read_note to find and read notes; vault_read_file for images, canvases, and other non-markdown files. Use vault_get_memory to retrieve user preferences and context from About Me/ files.

Vault content is Obsidian Flavored Markdown. No tools that modify the vault are available.

tools.name: vault_find_orphans
tools.title: Find Orphans
tools.description:
Find notes with no incoming links from other notes or canvases. A note that only links to itself still counts as an orphan.

Example: vault_find_orphans({})
Example: vault_find_orphans({ exclude_folders: ["Templates", "Archive"], limit: 20 })

When to use: Vault maintenance — surfacing notes to integrate into the graph.
Prefer vault_get_backlinks to check the connectivity of one specific note rather than scanning the whole vault.

Parameters:
- exclude_folders replaces the defaults, it does not add to them — list a default yourself to keep it. Pass [] for no exclusions. Each entry names a whole folder, subfolders included: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/", ignoring ASCII letter case. Excluded notes are left out of the results; links from them still count as incoming links. To keep the daily notes folder excluded, list it yourself: the folder named in Obsidian's Daily Notes settings, which vault_get_daily_note's path starts with.
- limit applies after exclusions and sorting; nothing in the response signals truncation; raise limit for more.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.

Errors:
- An empty array means no orphans were found (after exclusions), not an error.
- "too many excluded folders" — pass at most 994 exclude_folders entries, then retry.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata: path, title (the title property; file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (the tags property), body_tags (#tags in the note's text, one per spelling; absent when none), related ([] when missing), folder (top-level, "" at the root), type (null when missing or not text), created (null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (ISO 8601 file time), bytes (on-disk size), and when present leading_callout (the opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every property but title, type, created, related and tags). Sorted by most recently modified.

exclude_folders.description: Folder paths to exclude (e.g. Projects; default: the daily notes folder, "Templates", "About Me")

tools.name: vault_get_backlinks
tools.title: Get Backlinks
tools.description:
Find all notes and canvases that link to a given note or canvas — captures [[wikilinks]], [markdown](links), ![[embeds]], wikilinks inside properties (e.g. related:), and canvas cards that embed the file. Heading anchors ([[note#heading]]) and aliases ([[note|alias]]) resolve as backlinks to the base note. Links inside code blocks are ignored; a note linking to itself appears in its own backlinks.

Example: vault_get_backlinks({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_get_backlinks({ path: "Diagrams/architecture.canvas" })

When to use: Understanding what references a note or canvas, assessing its connectivity before editing or deleting, or finding related notes via the graph.
For outgoing links (what a note links TO), use vault_get_outgoing_links. To find notes nothing else links to, use vault_find_orphans.

Parameters:
- path: pass the target's own path, never a link's text: a link written as [[Note]], as a relative ../Note.md, or as a full path counts toward the note it resolves to.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds. A path nothing links to returns an empty result (count 0), not an error; if you expected links, find valid paths with vault_search, vault_list_notes, or vault_list_files.

Returns: JSON with path (the queried note or canvas), backlinks (every linking note and canvas, as { path, title, bytes } sorted by title; bytes is the source's on-disk size), and count.

Errors:
- "path must end in …" — add the .md or .canvas extension
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

path.description: Exact vault-relative path including .md or .canvas extension (e.g. "Projects/vault-cortex.md"). Case-sensitive.

tools.name: vault_get_daily_note
tools.title: Get Daily Note
tools.description:
Read a daily note by date, using the vault's configured Daily Notes folder and filename date format.

Example: vault_get_daily_note({ date: "2026-05-13" })
Example: vault_get_daily_note({}) — returns today's daily note

When to use: When you need today's or a specific date's daily note. For recent vault activity, vault_recent_notes lists the most recently changed notes; it has no date filter.

Parameters:
- date: always YYYY-MM-DD, whatever filename format the vault uses; past and future dates are both valid.

Errors:
- "invalid date …" / "… is not a calendar date" — pass a real date in YYYY-MM-DD form (2026-02-30 is refused)
- "daily note format contains unsupported token(s): ..." — the configured date format contains tokens the server cannot reproduce; ask the vault's owner to change the format in Obsidian, or the server's operator to set DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT (the message names the tokens)
- "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" / "absolute path blocked" — the configured daily notes folder or format leads outside the vault or into a hidden folder; ask the vault's owner to change it in Obsidian, or the server's operator to set DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER and DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …" or another filesystem error — the message says what to do

Returns: JSON with path (string — resolved vault-relative path), content (string|null — the note's full text, properties block included, or null when the note doesn't exist), and exists (boolean).

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. "2026-05-13", "2025-12-31"). Defaults to today in the server's timezone.

tools.name: vault_get_memory
tools.title: Get Memory
tools.description:
Read semantic memory from About Me/ files. Each file holds dated bullet entries under H2 headings. With file: that file. With file+section: just that H2 section's entries. With file+on_or_after: only the entries dated on or after that date, from one H2 section when section is given and otherwise from every section.

Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Principles" }) — the whole file
Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Principles", section: "Decision heuristics (newest first)" })
Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Opinions", section: "Code patterns", on_or_after: "2026-09-01" })
Example: vault_get_memory({ file: "Opinions", on_or_after: "2026-09-01" }) — every section's entries since the date

When to use: Reading user preferences, principles, opinions, or other persistent context stored in About Me/ files. Call vault_list_memory_files first to discover valid file and section names.
Prefer vault_read_note for reading non-memory notes. To find entries by topic across every file, use vault_memory_recall.

Behavior:
- No args reads every file, joined by --- lines, which can be large.
- Entries come back in document order, newest first by default.

Errors:
- "section requires a file" / "on_or_after requires a file" — add file
- "memory file not found" — call vault_list_memory_files to discover valid names
- "memory file must not start with a dot" / "… must be a bare name without path separators" / "… must be named without .md" — each message names the part of the name to drop
- "section not found: …" — no H2 heading matches; the message lists the file's sections
- "date must be a real ISO calendar date" — on_or_after must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date
- "cannot read memory file …" / "cannot list memory folder …" — a memory file, or the About Me/ folder itself on a call without file, can't be read: check file against vault_list_memory_files and shorten an over-long name; otherwise ask the vault's owner to check the folder

Returns: Without on_or_after, raw markdown with the properties block stripped, or an empty string when no memory files exist yet. With on_or_after, JSON { entries, total, on_or_after } where each entry is { file, section, date, text } — text is the raw entry markdown (bullet + continuation lines, wikilinks intact). An empty match returns { entries: [], total: 0, on_or_after }.

file.description: Memory file name without .md (e.g. "Principles", "Opinions"). Use the exact letter case.

section.description: H2 section heading (e.g. "Decision heuristics (newest first)"). Matched case-insensitively, with or without the "(newest first)" suffix.

tools.name: vault_get_outgoing_links
tools.title: Get Outgoing Links
tools.description:
Find all notes and files a given note or canvas links to. For notes: [[wikilinks]], [markdown](links), ![[embeds]], and wikilinks inside properties (e.g. related:). For canvas files: file nodes, not links inside text cards. Links inside code blocks are ignored; self-links are included. Each target is listed once, however often the note links to it.

Example: vault_get_outgoing_links({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_get_outgoing_links({ path: "Diagrams/architecture.canvas" })

When to use: Navigating the graph forward, auditing broken links in one note or canvas, or checking dependencies before editing.
For incoming links (what links TO a note), use vault_get_backlinks.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds. A path that does not exist, or one in a dot-prefixed folder, returns an empty result (count 0), not an error, just as a note with no outbound links does; if you expected links, find valid paths with vault_search, vault_list_notes, or vault_list_files.

Returns: JSON with path, outgoing_links (every link target, as { path, title, exists, kind, bytes, daily_note_forward_ref } sorted by target path), and count. A target's path is the vault-relative path the link resolved to; a broken link's path is its target text without any #heading or |alias, with a markdown link's %-escapes decoded. When exists is true, kind "note" is a markdown note readable via vault_read_note and kind "file" a non-markdown file (.canvas, image, PDF) readable via vault_read_file; when exists is false the link is broken and kind is "note" even for a path like "diagram.png". title is null for files and broken links. daily_note_forward_ref is true on a broken link into the daily notes folder (a daily note not yet created, not breakage) and false otherwise, including when Obsidian's Daily Notes folder setting is the vault root or blank. bytes is the on-disk size (null for broken links), not the delivery cost: vault_read_file downscales a large image to fit response limits.

Errors:
- "path must end in …" — add the .md or .canvas extension
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

path.description: Exact vault-relative path including .md or .canvas extension (e.g. "Projects/vault-cortex.md"). Case-sensitive.

tools.name: vault_list_files
tools.title: List Files
tools.description:
List non-markdown files in the vault or a folder — images, canvases, PDFs, data files — with per-file byte sizes and per-extension counts.

Example: vault_list_files({}) — non-markdown files across the whole vault
Example: vault_list_files({ folder: "attachments" })
Example: vault_list_files({ extensions: [".png", ".jpg"], limit: 20 })

When to use: discovering what files exist before reading them with vault_read_file. vault_list_notes and vault_search_by_folder cover only markdown notes, and beyond notes vault_search indexes only canvas, PDF, and text-format files, so this is the discovery surface for everything else. For the files one specific note links to, prefer vault_get_outgoing_links.

Behavior: Use the folder's exact letter case; a different case can find nothing. Hidden (dot-prefixed) files and folders, .obsidian/ among them, never appear.

Errors:
- A visible folder containing no files — or one that doesn't exist, or a path that names a file — returns an empty listing, not an error.
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — the folder is absolute, escapes the vault, names the vault root itself (e.g. "."), or is hidden like ".obsidian"; use a vault-relative folder outside hidden folders, and omit folder to list the whole vault.
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …" or another filesystem error — the message names the folder it could not read, and what to do; until then, pass a folder outside it.

Returns: JSON with files (array of { path, extension, bytes }, sorted by path; extension is "(none)" for a file without one), extension_counts (counts keyed by extension, e.g. { ".png": 3 }, over the full filtered set), total (full filtered count), and truncated (true when total exceeds limit).

Readable types: vault_read_file reads only images (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp), .canvas, .pdf, and the text formats .svg/.json/.txt/.csv/.xml/.log/.yaml/.yml/.base.

folder.description: Folder path to search recursively (e.g. "attachments" or "Projects/media"). Omit to list the whole vault.

extensions.description: Only include these extensions, case-insensitive, leading dot optional (e.g. [".png", "jpg"]).

tools.name: vault_list_memory_files
tools.title: List Memory Files
tools.description:
Discovery tool — lists About Me/ memory files with each file's heading outline, per-section entry counts, and leading callout. Does NOT return actual entries.

Example: vault_list_memory_files()

When to use: Discovering what memory files and sections exist — and what each file is for — BEFORE calling vault_get_memory. To find entries by topic instead, use vault_memory_recall.

Behavior: Lists every .md file directly inside About Me/, sorted by file name. Subfolders are not read, and hidden (dot-prefixed) files are skipped.

Errors:
- An empty or nonexistent memory folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "cannot list memory folder …" — a file stands at the memory folder's path, or its permissions block the server; ask the vault's owner to fix it
- "cannot read memory file …" — one listed file can't be read, which fails the whole listing; retry once, then ask the vault's owner to check that file

Returns: JSON array of file outlines, each { file, title, bytes, entry_policy, leading_callout, headings } — file is the name the other memory tools take as file (no .md); title is the title property, or file when there is none; bytes is the on-disk file size; headings lists H1 and H2 headings in order, each { level, text }, with entry_count on H2s; leading_callout is the top-of-file callout ({ type, title, body }; by convention a "Scope of this file" block describing what belongs in the file), or null; entry_policy is "append-only" (the default: by convention, entries are never edited or deleted) or "living" (a current-state file whose expired entries may be pruned; declared by an `entry-policy` property). The server does not enforce either policy.

tools.name: vault_list_notes
tools.title: List Notes
tools.description:
List the vault's note (.md) paths, optionally filtered by folder and/or glob pattern. Returns paths only — not content or metadata.

Example: vault_list_notes({ folder: "Projects" })
Example: vault_list_notes({ glob: "**/*session-log*.md" })
Example: vault_list_notes({ folder: "Projects", glob: "*.md" }) — the folder's top-level notes only

When to use: Browsing what exists in a folder by filename, or finding notes matching a path pattern.
Prefer vault_search_by_folder when you need metadata (tags, type, related) along with paths. Prefer vault_search for content-based discovery. Use vault_read_note to read a note from the results.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder; without a glob, notes in its subfolders are listed too: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/". Use the folder's exact letter case; a different case can find nothing.
- glob matches each note's path inside folder (its vault-relative path when folder is omitted), case-sensitively. * stays within one folder level and ** spans any depth: with folder "Projects", "**/*.md" lists every note under it.

Behavior: Paths come back sorted by vault-relative path in code-unit order (uppercase before lowercase). Hidden (dot-prefixed) notes and folders are never listed.

Errors:
- A nonexistent folder or no glob matches returns an empty array, not an error.
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — use a vault-relative folder outside hidden folders, or omit folder to list the whole vault.
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …" or another filesystem error — the message names the folder it could not read, and what to do; until then, pass a folder outside it.

Returns: JSON array of every matching vault-relative path (e.g. ["Notes/idea.md", "Projects/plan.md"]).

tools.name: vault_list_property_keys
tools.title: List Property Keys
tools.description:
Discover all property keys in the vault with note counts and sample values, without reading individual notes.

Example: vault_list_property_keys() returns [{ key: "tags", count: 342, sample_values: ["session-log", "project"] }, ...]
Example: vault_list_property_keys({ folder: "Projects" }) — the keys used under Projects/ only

When to use: Discovering what properties exist before searching by property. Good first step for vault orientation alongside vault_list_tags.
Prefer vault_list_property_values when you need the full list of values for a specific key. Prefer vault_search_by_property to find notes matching a specific key-value pair.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder, subfolders included: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/", ignoring ASCII letter case; omit it to scan the entire vault.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.
- Only properties count; inline Dataview fields (key:: value) are not listed.
- count is the number of notes that have the key, including notes where its value is empty (null).
- sample_values are the key's 3 most frequent values as text (a number as JavaScript prints it, so 1.0 lists as "1"; a checkbox as "1" or "0"), counting each array element separately; null values are skipped.

Errors:
- An empty vault or folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of { key, count, sample_values } sorted by count descending, then by key.

tools.name: vault_list_property_values
tools.title: List Property Values
tools.description:
List distinct values for a specific property key with how often each occurs.

Example: vault_list_property_values({ key: "status" }) returns [{ value: "done", count: 211 }, { value: "active", count: 47 }, ...]
Example: vault_list_property_values({ key: "tags", limit: 10 }) — the 10 most-used tags property values

When to use: Enumerating possible values for a property key before calling vault_search_by_property. Call vault_list_property_keys first to discover valid key names. A value listed here can be passed straight to vault_search_by_property, which matches text exactly and a complete number numerically too, so value "1" finds the number 1, the text "1", and a checked checkbox.

Parameters:
- key is case-sensitive and must match exactly as returned by vault_list_property_keys.
- folder names a whole folder, subfolders included: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/", ignoring ASCII letter case.
- limit keeps the most-used values; nothing in the response signals truncation; raise limit for more.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.
- Array elements (tags: ["a", "b"]) are counted individually, so the sum of counts may exceed the note count.
- Each value is listed as text, and values with the same text share one row with combined occurrence counts: number 1 and text "1" count together, while text "1.0" stays separate.
- Checkbox true and false come back as "1" and "0", counted with the numbers 1 and 0.
- null values are skipped.

Errors:
- An unknown key or empty folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of { value, count } sorted by count descending, then by value in binary text order ("10" before "2").

tools.name: vault_list_tags
tools.title: List Tags
tools.description:
List all tags in the vault with note counts, ordered by count descending, then by tag name.

Example: vault_list_tags() returns [{ tag: "session-log", count: 42 }, { tag: "project/vault-cortex", count: 8 }, ...]

When to use: Discovering what tags exist before searching by tag. Good first step for vault orientation.
Prefer vault_search_by_tag once you know which tag to query. To count tags property values in one folder, or only the most-used ones, use vault_list_property_values({ key: "tags" }) with folder or limit; it does not count #tags in note bodies.

Behavior:
- Tags in the tags property and #tags written in note bodies both count, and count is unique notes, not occurrences.
- Spellings that differ only in letter case are one tag, shown as the spelling written most often.
- Each hierarchical tag appears as one full entry, not split into segments.
- Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.

Errors:
- A vault with no tagged notes returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of { tag, count } holding every tag in the vault; tag omits the "#" prefix.

tools.name: vault_list_tasks
tools.title: List Tasks
tools.description:
List checkbox tasks across the whole vault with structured filters — the Tasks-plugin data model over MCP. Both task metadata formats are indexed: emoji signifiers (📅 due, ⏫ priority, 🔁 recurrence, ...) and Dataview inline fields ([due:: 2026-07-04], [priority:: high], ...). Task lines inside fenced code blocks and %% %% comment blocks are not indexed. Checkboxes typed NON_TASK in the Tasks plugin's status settings are also excluded.

Example: vault_list_tasks({ due: { before: "2026-07-04" } }) — overdue triage; the default status (not_done) and sort (due ascending) make this the "what's overdue?" call
Example: vault_list_tasks({ path: "Code Projects/vault-cortex/TASKS.md", heading: ["Active", "Up Next", "Waiting On"], sort_by: "position" }) — actionable Kanban lanes in board order
Example: vault_list_tasks({ folder: "Code Projects/vault-cortex" }) — all open tasks across a project tree (TASKS.md + task-notes/ subdirectories)
Example: vault_list_tasks({ status: "done", done: { after: "2026-06-26" } }) — what got completed this week

When to use: Reading task status and order on one board (path + sort_by: "position"; add status: "all" to include done and cancelled cards). Also any vault-wide task triage question — "what's overdue?", "what's open per project?", "what did I finish this week?" — in one call instead of per-board reads.
Prefer vault_read_note (heading mode) only when you need a lane's verbatim Markdown or a task's state right after a write. Prefer vault_search for full-text queries over note content.

Behavior: A file change takes a few seconds to appear here.

Parameters:
- status: "not_done" and "all" expand in arrays — ["not_done", "done"] matches todo + in_progress + done.
- due / scheduled / start / done / created / cancelled: a date filter only matches tasks that HAVE that date.
- folder: a whole folder, subfolders included ("Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/"), ignoring ASCII letter case.
- sort_by: a task with none of a date sort's dates comes last; "priority" ascending puts highest first, and tasks with no priority sort between medium and low.

Errors:
- "invalid due.before date: …" (any date filter's bound) — the bound isn't in YYYY-MM-DD form; use that form
- "… is not a calendar date" — a date filter's bound has the YYYY-MM-DD form but names a day that doesn't exist, such as 2026-02-30; pass a real date
- "path must end in …" — add the .md extension
- "tag must not be empty …" — tag is "#" alone; pass the tag name
- No matches returns { total: 0, tasks: [] }, not an error
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON { total, tasks }. Every task carries path, line, status, status_char (the checkbox character, such as "x" or "/"), description, folder (the task note's parent folder), depth (0 for top-level, 1+ for sub-tasks), is_kanban_task (true when the task's note has kanban-plugin in its properties), depends_on, and tags (the arrays are [] when empty). Every other field appears only when the task has it: heading (nearest heading above the task), created/scheduled/start/due/done/cancelled dates, priority, recurrence, on_completion, task_id, block_id, parent_block_id (sub-tasks whose parent carries a ^block-id), done_lanes (Kanban boards only: the headings of the lanes whose first line is **Complete**), and subtask_progress ({ done, total } over the task's DIRECT checklist children; done counts status "done" only, a cancelled child counts toward total, and the counts ignore the query's filters).

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

priority.description: Priority levels, OR-combined; "none" selects tasks with no priority signifier

tag.description: Tag on the task line, "#" optional; matches nested tags, any letter case

heading.description: Exact heading text or array of headings, OR-combined, case-sensitive (e.g. "Active" or ["Active", "Up Next"])

path.description: Restrict to one note (vault-relative path ending ".md", case-sensitive)

top_level_only.description: When true, only top-level tasks (depth 0) are returned — excludes indented sub-tasks and checklist items. Default false.

limit.description: Max results (default 50); total always reports the full match count

sort_by.description: Sort key (default "due"). Date sorts cascade through related fields when the primary is absent (through the rest of due → scheduled → start → created, in that order; done does not cascade). "position" sorts by file path then line number.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction. Default per field: "asc" for due/scheduled/priority/position, "desc" for start/created/done/note_mtime. When a date sort cascades (see sort_by), each field uses its own default direction; an explicit value overrides all fields uniformly.

tools.name: vault_memory_recall
tools.title: Memory Recall
tools.description:
Recall memory entries about a topic — entry-granular hybrid (keyword + semantic) retrieval across ALL About Me/ files and ALL time. Returns the relevant dated entries, up to limit, sorted oldest-first — semantic matching finds early entries even when their phrasing differs from the query. Tuned for recall over precision: expect some marginal entries. Content-word queries ("testing philosophy", "sustainable pacing") rank best. A meta-framed query ("opinions on testing") that scores below the relevance threshold degrades to any-term keyword matching instead of returning nothing.

Example: vault_memory_recall({ query: "working hours and pacing" })
Example: vault_memory_recall({ query: "testing philosophy", file: "Opinions" })

When to use: Answering "what does my memory say about X?" or "how has my view on Y evolved?" — topic-based recall across memory files. Prefer vault_get_memory to read a known file or section verbatim; prefer vault_search for notes outside the memory layer.

Behavior: A memory file change takes a few seconds to appear here.

Errors:
- No matching entries returns entries: [] and total: 0, not an error
- An unknown file returns empty results — call vault_list_memory_files to discover valid names
- "[SqliteError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON { entries, total, truncated, search_mode, reranked }. Each entry is { file, section, date, text } — text is the raw entry markdown (wikilinks intact, continuation lines included); file and section feed directly into vault_get_memory. The total counts every matched entry; truncated=true means limit dropped the least-relevant matches, whatever their dates, so raise limit or narrow the query for the complete set. With file, limit keeps the most relevant matches from that file. search_mode is "hybrid" when semantic matching contributed and "fts" when keyword matching alone did, the any-term fallback included; reranked is true when the reranker ran.

query.description: Topic to recall, in natural language.

file.description: Restrict to one memory file, name without .md (e.g. "Opinions"), in its exact letter case. Omit for cross-file recall — the default and usual choice.

tools.name: vault_read_file
tools.title: Read File
tools.description:
Read a non-markdown vault file in its most useful form per type — the read-side companion to vault_read_note for everything that isn't a note.

Example: vault_read_file({ path: "attachments/diagram.png" }) — the image itself, shrunk when too large
Example: vault_read_file({ path: "Boards/Roadmap.canvas" }) — a readable outline of the canvas
Example: vault_read_file({ path: "exports/data.json" }) — the file content as text
Example: vault_read_file({ path: "exports/big.csv", limit: 500 }) — the first 500 lines
Example: vault_read_file({ path: "papers/research.pdf" }) — structured text with title, headings, and links

When to use: whenever a note references a file you need to actually see or read — an embedded diagram, a linked canvas, data file, or PDF. Find the files a note links to (with byte sizes) via vault_get_outgoing_links. Browse a folder's files via vault_list_files. vault_search also indexes canvas, PDF, and text-format content, but not images or other files. For .md notes use vault_read_note. To check a large file's line count before reading it whole, request start_line: 1 with limit: 1 — one line plus the total.

Parameters:
- raw: true switches a canvas or PDF to its other form. A canvas returns its exact JSON source (geometry, ids, colors) instead of the outline. A PDF returns each page rendered as an image instead of extracted text, showing layout, diagrams, tables, and formatting; only the first 5 pages are rendered, and later pages are readable only as text, without raw.
- start_line and limit page any text result as a line window. The text output cap (a fixed 100 KiB) applies to each window, so one very long line can still overflow it; paging never gets around the file-size cap.

Behavior: A paged window comes back with \n line endings and no trailing newline, preceded by a metadata line stating the window, the total line count, and where to continue ("data.csv — lines 51–100 of 400 (continue with start_line: 101)"); an unpaged read of a text format returns the file byte-exact.

Errors:
- "not a file: … is a markdown note" — the path ends in .md; read notes with vault_read_note
- "file not found" — no file exists at that path (a folder is not a file); discover valid paths via vault_list_files
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — pass a vault-relative path with no dot-prefixed part
- "file too large" — the file exceeds the file-size cap (MAX_FILE_BYTES, default 50 MiB), which the server's operator can raise
- "text output too large" — a text file, canvas, or PDF renders past the text output cap; page it with start_line and limit, or reduce limit when a single window overflows
- "start line past the end" — start_line exceeds the file's line count; the error states the total, so retry with a smaller start_line
- "line range is not available" (start_line or limit on an image, or on a PDF read with raw: true) / "raw source is not available for images" (raw on an image) — drop that input
- "not valid UTF-8" — the file's bytes aren't UTF-8 text; ask for a UTF-8 copy
- "invalid .canvas JSON" — the canvas file is empty or not valid JSON; set raw: true to read its source as text
- "PDF has no extractable text" — the PDF contains no text (scanned or image-only); the error states the page count. Set raw: true to render pages as images instead
- "PDF is password-protected" — read an unprotected copy instead
- "PDF is damaged or not a PDF" / "could not decode image" — the PDF does not parse, or the image is empty, damaged, not an image despite its extension, or over about 268 million pixels; any other PDF or image error comes back in the reading library's own words. Replace or re-export the file
- "PDF page rendering failed" — read it without raw: true to get its text instead; if that read also finds no text, this tool can't read the PDF
- "image cannot be fitted into …" — the image is over the image output budget even after shrinking; ask the server's operator to raise MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …" or another filesystem error — the message says what to do
- "file changed while reading" — retry the read
- "PDF reader could not start" — the server's PDF reader failed to load; retry once, then ask the server's operator to restart the server
- "unsupported file type …" — the type (audio, archives, …) is not readable; the error names the readable types plus the file's existence and size

Returns: by file type:
- Images (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp): an image content block plus a one-line metadata text block. The image is downscaled and recompressed when it exceeds the image output budget (49152 bytes) or has a longer side over 1568 pixels; an animated GIF is reduced to its first frame when recompressed.
- Canvas (.canvas): one text block holding a readable markdown outline — groups, node content in reading order, and a connections list with edge labels.
- PDFs (.pdf): one text block of structured text with document metadata — title, page count, heading hierarchy, code blocks and inline code, page separators, and a links footer; with raw: true, a metadata text block followed by alternating image and text blocks (one pair per page).
- Text formats (.svg/.json/.txt/.csv/.xml/.log/.yaml/.yml/.base): one text block holding the file content verbatim.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the file, including its extension (e.g. "attachments/photo.png", "Boards/Roadmap.canvas"). Must NOT end in ".md". Use the exact letter case.

raw.description: Return a canvas's or PDF's alternative form. Changes nothing for text formats.

tools.name: vault_read_note
tools.title: Read Note
tools.description:
Read a markdown note by its vault-relative path. By default returns the full raw content including properties; optional modes return just the properties, just the heading outline, or just one section.

Example: vault_read_note({ path: "Projects/vault-cortex.md" })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", outline: true })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Active" })
Example: vault_read_note({ path: "TASKS.md", heading: "Done", start_line: 1, limit: 20 })

When to use: You know the exact path and need a specific note's content. For a large note (a long Kanban board or doc), use outline: true to see its headings and any text sitting above them, then heading: "..." to read just the one section you need. For a note or section too long for one response, page it with start_line and limit to read a window at a time. To check a note's or section's line count, request start_line: 1 with limit: 1 — one line plus the total.
Prefer vault_search when you don't know the path. For task status or order on a board, prefer vault_list_tasks; heading mode returns a lane's Markdown. Prefer vault_get_memory for About Me/ files (returns content without properties). To explore what links to this note or what it links to, use vault_get_backlinks and vault_get_outgoing_links.

Behavior: a section spans from its heading to the next heading with the same or a smaller level number (or EOF), so it includes its child headings. Empty headings ("##" with no text) act as boundaries but cannot be targeted; read the parent section or the full note.

Errors:
- "note not found" — no note exists at this path; verify it with vault_list_notes
- "heading not found" — the message lists the available headings
- "ambiguous heading" — multiple headings match; use heading_level to disambiguate, or read the full note (omit heading) when headings share the same level
- "outline, heading, and properties_only are mutually exclusive — set at most one"
- "heading_level requires a heading" — pass heading with it
- "heading cannot be empty" — heading is whitespace only; pass the heading's text
- "line paging is not available in outline mode" / "… properties_only mode" — start_line and limit page only a full read or a heading section
- "start line past the end" — the message states the line count; resend a start_line within it
- 'path must end in ".md"' — add the extension to a note's path; read other files (images, .canvas, data files) with vault_read_file
- "absolute path blocked" / "path traversal blocked" / "hidden path blocked" — pass a vault-relative path with no dot-prefixed part
- "properties block is not valid YAML …" — only properties_only raises it; a full read, outline and heading still work; the error says how to repair it
- "ENAMETOOLONG: …" or another filesystem error — the message says what to do

Returns: Raw markdown string (default); JSON object of properties, {} when the note has none (properties_only); JSON outline object, shaped as the outline parameter describes (outline); raw markdown of the section, heading line included (heading). When start_line or limit is given, the result is preceded by a window-metadata text block ("path — lines 1–20 of 250 (continue with start_line: 21)"). Unpaged full reads return the file's exact bytes; heading sections and paged reads use LF line endings. In the outline, bytes at the root is the whole file's size, modified its modification time (ISO 8601), and each heading's bytes the size of the text heading mode returns for that section; an empty heading appears with text: "".

path.description: Vault-relative path to the note, including the ".md" extension (e.g. "About Me/Principles.md"). Use the exact letter case.

properties_only.description: If true, returns parsed properties as JSON instead of full note content

outline.description: If true, returns { bytes, modified, leading_callout?, leading_content?, headings } as JSON instead of body content. headings: [{ level, text, bytes }]; leading_callout: { type, title, body } when the note has a top-of-file callout; leading_content: the rest of the body text above the first heading (callout lines excluded) when the note has any.

heading.description: Return only this section. Case-sensitive exact match.

heading_level.description: Heading level (1-6) for disambiguation when multiple headings share the same text

tools.name: vault_recent_notes
tools.title: Recent Notes
tools.description:
List recently modified or created notes, sorted by timestamp — a time-ordered window into the vault, not a date-range filter.

Example: vault_recent_notes({ limit: 10 })
Example: vault_recent_notes({ sort_by: "created", limit: 5 })

When to use: Catching up on vault changes, finding recent work, or orienting after a break.
Prefer vault_search for content-based discovery, including a text query limited to a date range (its created and modified filters). Prefer vault_search_by_folder for browsing a specific folder.

Parameters:
- sort_by "modified" uses filesystem mtime. Any file write counts (content edits, property changes, sync touches), so recently-synced notes appear recent even without user edits.
- sort_by "created" uses the created property; notes where it is missing or not an ISO date sort after every dated note, so a small limit can leave them out — use "modified" to see them.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.

Errors:
- An empty vault returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata: path, title (the title property; file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (the tags property), body_tags (#tags in the note's text, one per spelling; absent when none), related ([] when missing), folder (top-level, "" at the root), type (null when missing or not text), created (null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (ISO 8601 file time), bytes (on-disk size), and when present leading_callout (the opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every property but title, type, created, related and tags). Newest first by the sort_by timestamp.

tools.name: vault_search
tools.title: Search Notes
tools.description:
Hybrid search across vault notes and file content (canvas, PDF, and text files), ranked by combined keyword and semantic relevance. Semantic matching finds notes even when exact keywords differ — "career aspirations" finds notes about "goals" and "targets". Unquoted terms use implicit AND with stemming ("running" also matches "run"); wrap in double quotes for exact phrases; punctuated terms (vault-cortex, deploy/local) are matched as exact adjacent-word phrases.

Filters — all conditions AND-combine with each other and the text query; any filter but folder returns notes only:
- folder: a whole folder, subfolders included: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/", ignoring ASCII letter case
- tags: every listed tag must match, in the tags property or as a #tag in the body, in any letter case; "project" also matches "project/a"
- type: the type property, matched exactly, letter case included
- related: every listed link must appear in the related property, written as it is there, brackets and alias included
- properties: keys and text values match exactly, letter case included; values compare by exact type — pass a number as a number, not "4". Exception: true and false compare as 1 and 0, so true or 1 matches a checked checkbox and the number 1. A list property matches when any element equals the value.
- created / modified: bounds compare whole calendar days in the server's time zone (returned created and modified values show its UTC offset). A note whose created property is missing or not an ISO date never matches a created filter

Example: vault_search({ query: "how the server watches for file changes" })
Example: vault_search({ query: "kubernetes networking", filters: { tags: ["reference"] } })
Example: vault_search({ query: "meeting notes", filters: { type: "meeting", folder: "Work" } })
Example: vault_search({ query: "decision", filters: { modified: { after: "2026-06-30" } } }) — matching notes touched in July or later

When to use: The primary discovery tool for content-based queries, optionally constrained by metadata.
Prefer vault_search_by_tag for tag-only queries without text. Prefer vault_search_by_folder for browsing a folder. Prefer vault_search_by_property for metadata-only queries. Prefer vault_recent_notes for time-based browsing.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds. When only keyword matching ran (search_mode "fts"), at most 100 notes and 100 files come back; with "hybrid", at most 200 notes and 200 files.

Errors:
- No matches returns an empty results array with total 0, not an error
- Malformed query syntax never throws: the words AND, OR, NOT and NEAR in any letter case, and punctuation such as *, ^, parentheses and colons, are dropped before keyword matching; a query left with no terms is matched by meaning only, or finds nothing when only keyword matching ran (search_mode "fts")
- "invalid created.on date: …" or "… is not a calendar date" (any created/modified bound) — pass a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form
- "tag must not be empty …" — a tags entry is only "#"; pass the tag name
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON with results array (path, title, snippet, score, tags (the tags property), body_tags (#tags in the note's text, one per spelling; absent when none), folder (a note's top-level folder; a file's full parent folder), type, kind, extension, created, modified, bytes), total (results returned, not all matches), search_mode ("hybrid" when vector embeddings contributed, "fts" when only keyword matching ran), and reranked (true when a second ranking pass reordered the results). A higher score is more relevant. kind is "note" or, for non-markdown content, "file", which also carries extension (e.g. ".pdf"). created is omitted, not null, when a result has none; type is null when the result has no type property; bytes is the on-disk size. With include_leading_callout, each result also carries leading_callout (the opening callout, { type, title, body }) when present.

properties.description: Match arbitrary properties by key-value (e.g. { status: "active", priority: 1 })

created.description: Created date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD) on the "created" property

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

modified.description: Modified date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD) on filesystem modified time

before.description: Exclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly earlier dates

after.description: Exclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD) — strictly later dates

snippet_tokens.description: Snippet length in words, not model tokens (default 30)

include_leading_callout.description: If true, include each result's leading callout.

tools.name: vault_search_by_folder
tools.title: Search by Folder
tools.description:
Browse notes in a folder with full metadata.

Example: vault_search_by_folder({ folder: "Projects" })
Example: vault_search_by_folder({ folder: "About Me", recursive: false, limit: 10 }) — the folder's own notes, 10 most recent

When to use: Exploring a folder's contents with full context for vault orientation.
Prefer vault_list_notes when you only need paths. Prefer vault_search when you have a text query. Use vault_get_backlinks or vault_get_outgoing_links to explore how notes in a folder connect to the rest of the vault.

Parameters:
- folder names a whole folder, subfolders included: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/", ignoring ASCII letter case; a trailing slash is ignored. With recursive: false, only the folder's own notes are kept.
- limit keeps the most recently modified notes. There is no offset, and nothing in the response signals truncation; raise limit for more.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds. Notes in hidden (dot-prefixed) folders never appear.

Errors:
- An empty or nonexistent folder returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata: path, title (the title property; file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (the tags property), body_tags (#tags in the note's text, one per spelling; absent when none), related ([] when missing), folder (top-level, "" at the root), type (null when missing or not text), created (null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (ISO 8601 file time), bytes (on-disk size), and when present leading_callout (the opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every property but title, type, created, related and tags). Sorted by most recently modified, then by path.

tools.name: vault_search_by_property
tools.title: Search by Property
tools.description:
Find notes where a property matches a value.

Example: vault_search_by_property({ key: "status", value: "in-progress" })
Example: vault_search_by_property({ key: "type", value: "session-log", folder: "Code Projects" })

When to use: Finding notes by metadata when you don't have a text query.
Prefer vault_search when you also have a text query (it supports property filters too). Prefer vault_search_by_tag for tag-specific queries (it matches nested tags and #tags in note bodies; key "tags" here matches only the tags property). Use vault_list_property_keys to discover valid keys and vault_list_property_values to see what values a key takes.

Parameters:
- key and value both match exactly and case-sensitively, with no partial matching or globbing; value matches a stored text value as written.
- A value written as a complete, finite YAML 1.2 core number (-4, 04, .5, 4., 1e3, 0x1F, 0o17) also matches stored numbers numerically: "04" and "4.0" match number 4 and their own literal text, but not text "4". Anything else ("4abc", " 4", 0b binary) matches only as text.
- A checkbox matches only as text: pass "1" (checked) or "0" (unchecked); "1.0" and "true" do not match.
- A list property matches when an element equals value in full: "blog" matches tags: ["blog", "draft"] but not tags: ["my-blog"].
- folder names a whole folder, subfolders included: "Projects" covers "Projects/Archive" but not "ProjectsOld/", ignoring ASCII letter case; omit it to search the entire vault.
- limit keeps the most recently modified matches; nothing in the response signals truncation; raise limit for more.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.

Errors:
- An unknown key or unmatched value returns an empty array, not an error.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata: path, title (the title property; file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (the tags property), body_tags (#tags in the note's text, one per spelling; absent when none), related ([] when missing), folder (top-level, "" at the root), type (null when missing or not text), created (null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (ISO 8601 file time), bytes (on-disk size), and when present leading_callout (the opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every property but title, type, created, related and tags). Sorted by most recently modified (any file write, so a recently-synced note can sort ahead of an older edit), then by path.

tools.name: vault_search_by_tag
tools.title: Search by Tag
tools.description:
Find notes by tag, in the tags property or as a #tag in the body, ignoring letter case. Unless exact is true, a tag also matches every tag nested under it at any depth: "project" matches "project/vault-cortex" and "project/a/b". A nested tag continues with "/", so "project" never matches "projects" or "my-project".

Example: vault_search_by_tag({ tag: "project" })
Example: vault_search_by_tag({ tag: "project", exact: true, limit: 50 }) — notes tagged "project" itself, up to 50

When to use: Tag-only lookups, for one tag or a whole tag hierarchy, with no text query. Use vault_list_tags first to discover available tags.
Prefer vault_search when you need text-based relevance ranking.

Parameters:
- tag: a trailing slash matches nothing ("project/" matches neither "project" nor "project/a"), so pass the tag name without it.
- limit keeps the most recently modified notes; nothing in the response signals truncation; raise limit for more.

Behavior: Results can lag a file change by a few seconds.

Errors:
- An unknown tag or no matches returns an empty array, not an error.
- "tag must not be empty …" — tag is "#" alone; pass the tag name.
- "[SqliteError]: …" / "[IndexIntegrityError]: …" — the index failed, not the call; the message says what to do

Returns: JSON array of note metadata: path, title (the title property; file name without .md when missing or not text), tags (the tags property), body_tags (#tags in the note's text, one per spelling; absent when none), related ([] when missing), folder (top-level, "" at the root), type (null when missing or not text), created (null when missing or not an ISO date), modified (ISO 8601 file time), bytes (on-disk size), and when present leading_callout (the opening callout, { type, title, body }) and additional_properties (every property but title, type, created, related and tags). Tags keep the note's letter case. Sorted by most recently modified, then by path.

exact.description: Match only the tag itself (default: false)

prompts.name: daily-review
prompts.title: Daily review & reconciliation
prompts.description: Reconcile a day — daily note, vault-wide task status (due/overdue, scheduled), modified notes, and links — surface what happened, what's open, and durable facts worth saving to About Me/ memory.

arguments.name: date
arguments.description: Day to review in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)

arguments.name: max_chars
arguments.description: Optional cap on embedded content length (characters); omit for full content

prompts.name: vault-orientation
prompts.title: Orient to this vault
prompts.description: Survey this vault's structure and health — stats, folders, tags, properties (with adoption rates), orphans, recent notes, and the About Me/ memory layer.
